blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Garden Village condos

items.t: Garden Village is in south-west Burnaby, west of Metrotown toward Boundary Road, around Central Park and Patterson Station; Heritage Burnaby places the Garden Village subdivision inside the Central Park historic neighbourhood, in the City's Maywood / Garden Village planning area.

The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS® sub-area; the historic subdivision was a 140-acre site developed from 1953, and the modern sub-area is generally the residential streets between Central Park / Boundary Road to the west, Kingsway to the north and the Metrotown side to the east.
Where the condos are: I don't know of any in the area.
The condo towers you can see from Garden Village streets, on Patterson Avenue and Central Boulevard beside Central Park, are listed in the Metrotown and Central Park areas, not Garden Village.

Transit anchors: Patterson Station, on the Expo Line at Patterson Avenue and Central Park, serves the sub-area's north side, and Metrotown Station, the next Expo Line station east, is the area's main bus exchange; route 116 links Metrotown Station south through the Sussex / Imperial streets toward Edmonds Station.
For all of Burnaby in September 2026, condos and townhomes had a median of $686,000, $763 per sq ft, 98% of list price and 36 days on the market. There's no median for Garden Village itself.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Garden Village

items.t: Burnaby zoning — the current bylaw is new: the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the former Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) — the 1965 bylaw is not current and must not be cited as such.
Burnaby OCP: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan was adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP, and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict.

The strata homes here are multiplexes, not towers: in June 2024, Burnaby combined its single- and two-family zones into one R1 zone that allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, and lots with two or more main units can be stratified. A stratified multiplex unit in Garden Village is a strata lot, so the Form B, depreciation report and reserve fund rules apply.

Burnaby property tax: 2026 taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Garden Village condos

items.t: There isn't really a Garden Village condo market. Garden Village had no condos or townhomes for sale in September 2026, and the towers you can see from its streets are listed in Metrotown and Central Park. If you're comparing "Garden Village condos", you're comparing buildings in other areas, under the same city rules but with their own sales figures.

Burnaby rewrote its entire zoning bylaw in 2026. The Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and replaced the 1965 bylaw outright — any listing copy, appraisal or older guide citing Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) district names for this area is citing a repealed bylaw.

The new OCP outranks the old neighbourhood plans. The Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict — check the 2050 map before assuming assembly or density value on a Kingsway-side lot.

The subdivision dates from one 1953 plan. Heritage Burnaby records that the Garden Village subdivision was started in 1953 with a plan to build 500 modern homes on the 140-acre site. That's why the interior streets look like one planned post-war subdivision, and why there are no older apartment buildings in it.

District energy is planned for the neighbouring centres, not this subdivision. Burnaby is creating a District Energy Utility to bring clean thermal energy from Metro Vancouver's Waste-to-Energy facility to homes and businesses, with service slated to be introduced in Metrotown and Edmonds, where almost half of Burnaby's residential growth over the next 20 years is expected.

Central Park is the amenity, and it is at the edge, not the centre. The City lists 12 tennis courts with lights and a practice wall at Central Park, immediately north-east of the sub-area — north-side addresses use it daily; Rumble Street–side addresses are a materially longer walk.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Garden Village

items.t: Garden Village history (Heritage Burnaby): subdivisions began appearing in the Central Park neighbourhood in the 1920s, growth slowed in the Depression and picked up in the post-war boom, and the Garden Village subdivision was started in 1953 with a plan to build 500 modern homes on the 140-acre site. Although the interurban line closed in 1953, the neighbourhood stayed an active commercial and residential centre. The land here is a completed 1953 subdivision of fee-simple lots.
Post-war subdivision house lots

The only lot-size figures are the R1 zone's thresholds (280 m² and 281 m²). The interior streets were built as one planned post-war subdivision, which is why two similar 1950s houses can be worth quite different amounts once you check, lot by lot, whether they're within 400 m of a frequent bus stop.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Garden Village.
Not counted — the Patterson / Central Park towers next door

Market figures, September 2026 (homes, not land): in Garden Village, 9 detached homes were listed and 1 sold (11%), with no condos or townhomes. Burnaby's medians were $1,825,000 for detached homes and $686,000 for condos and townhomes.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Garden Village lots

items.t: Garden Village is in southwest Burnaby, west of Metrotown toward Boundary Road, around Central Park and Patterson Station; Heritage Burnaby places the original Garden Village subdivision in the historic Central Park neighbourhood. It's also the real estate board's name for the area. The City doesn't publish a boundary; the original subdivision was a 140-acre site built from 1953, and today's area is roughly the streets between Central Park and Boundary Road to the west, Kingsway to the north and the Metrotown side to the east.

Nearby areas: Metrotown and Central Park to the east and north-east, Maywood within the same planning area, the City of Vancouver (Killarney / Central Park side) across Boundary Road to the west, South Slope and Royal Oak to the south-east.

Roads and transit: Kingsway runs east–west along the north edge, Boundary Road runs along the Vancouver border on the west, and Patterson Avenue and Imperial Street run through toward Metrotown. Patterson Station on the Expo Line, at Patterson Avenue and Central Park, serves the north side; Metrotown Station, the next stop east, is the main bus exchange, and route 116 runs from Metrotown Station south through Sussex and Imperial toward Edmonds Station.

Parks and services: Central Park, just northeast, is the big park (with 12 lit tennis courts and a practice wall); the Rumble Street Urban Trail runs south of the area, part of Burnaby's 70-plus kilometres of urban trails. The Bob Prittie Metrotown library and Bonsor Recreation Complex are on the Metrotown side, the Metrotown Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 102-4555 Kingsway, and Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street) is to the northeast.

items.t: Age of homes: the area was subdivided in 1953, so many houses are post-war, with later infill and rebuilds.

blocks.text: Good to know about Garden Village lots

items.t: The subdivision and the SkyTrain arrived in opposite directions (1953): Heritage Burnaby records the Garden Village subdivision was undertaken in 1953 — the same year the interurban line closed — yet the neighbourhood remained an active centre; today's station value comes from Patterson Station on the Expo Line at the north side, a later layer entirely.

The trail south of the lots was finished in phases: Phase 3 of the Rumble Street Urban Trail between McKay Ave and Royal Oak Ave was completed in late 2018, in a City trail network now over 70 kilometres — south-side lots back onto a finished multi-use link, not a promised one.

Be careful with school catchment examples here: the one School Locator check used 5455 Rumble Street, Burnaby South Secondary's own address, which is in the catchment for Nelson Elementary. That shows catchments go by address, not which school a Rumble Street house is in; check the specific address.

District energy is a Metrotown/Edmonds story, not a Garden Village one: Burnaby's District Energy Utility will introduce service in Metrotown and Edmonds, where almost half of Burnaby's residential growth over the next 20 years is expected — no Garden Village service is stated, so do not carry a district-energy claim into a Garden Village lot memo.
